clue.text: Small and sweet: that's Murphy

definitions.note: Murphy is an old slang word for a potato, from the Irish surname

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
pud is British slang for pudding, a sweet course

explanation.surface: Someone is describing a man called Murphy as short and sweet-natured.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy looks like a man's name, but it is the definition: old slang for a potato, from the Irish association with the crop.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal names for the potato, so the slang word swaps for the other slang word.

clue.text: Old man respected is ruler restored

parts.note: Sir is the respectful title given to a knighted man

explanation.surface: An elderly respected man is a monarch returned to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: the Egyptian god was murdered and brought back to life, becoming lord of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Egyptian myth the god was killed by Set, reassembled and revived, then reigned over the dead: a monarch brought back.

clue.text: Urchin and fish served up with a cake

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a muffin is a small cake

explanation.surface: A street child is served a fish dish alongside a cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns GAR into RAG in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a ragged, scruffy child of the streets.

clue.text: Talk about the French in Swiss Cottage?

definitions.note: a mountain house in the Alpine style, typical of Switzerland

indicators.note: about means one word goes around the other, here talk surrounding the French article

parts.note: to chat is to talk
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Swiss Cottage is a London district, so this reads as a chat about the French living there.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss Cottage is a district of north-west London, named after a pub; the question mark says to read it literally as a cottage in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden Alpine house is the typical rustic home of Switzerland.

clue.text: Writer doing philosophy the French way so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the words are judged by how they are pronounced

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way; add so to get rue-so

explanation.surface: A writer doing philosophy in a French manner, as one might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to speak' (from 'so to speak') says RUE + SO is said aloud; 'so' does double duty as a leaf. RUE is French for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was a Genevan author and political philosopher of the Enlightenment.

clue.text: Almost entirely lecherous American writer

indicators.note: almost entirely means the word is given in full except its final letter

parts.note: randy is British slang for lustful

explanation.surface: An American author described as almost wholly lustful.
explanation.walkthrough: RANDY is everyday British slang for sexually eager; drop its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayn Rand was the Russian-born American novelist of The Fountainhead and Atlas Shrugged.

clue.text: Yielding second prize showing fondness

parts.note: something soft yields to pressure
a pot is a trophy cup, a prize

explanation.surface: A runner-up's prize that gives way, shown as a sign of affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a soft spot for someone is an idiom for liking or being fond of them.

clue.text: Sorceress losing head causes irritation

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a witch is a female sorcerer

explanation.surface: A beheaded sorceress causes annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritating sensation on the skin, so it is a kind of irritation.

clue.text: Haiti cops dressed in pale green

indicators.note: dressed suggests the letters are arranged or prepared anew, like dressed stone

explanation.surface: Police officers in Haiti wear a light green uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' looks like it means clothed, but it signals rearranging HAITI COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour named after the nut's kernel is a soft, light green.

clue.text: U-boat moving around

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A submarine moving about the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are prepositions or adverbs meaning in the vicinity of, or approximately.

clue.text: Skin layer pinched in powder magazine

indicators.note: pinched in means the letters are taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A layer of skin gets nipped inside an ammunition store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinched in' points to the letters straddling powDER MAgazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Derma is the medical term for the dermis, the layer of skin beneath the epidermis.

clue.text: Desperate to survive drop

parts.note: to last is to survive or endure
to ditch is to drop or abandon

explanation.surface: Someone frantic to stay alive after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final desperate attempt.

clue.text: Attack unnamed Bahamian port officer

indicators.note: unnamed means the abbreviation N, for name, is removed

parts.note: Nassau is the capital and main port of the Bahamas
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: An anonymous official at a Bahamas harbour is set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' takes N (name) out of NASSAU, leaving ASSAU.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent attack, as noun or verb.

clue.text: Fabulist initially adopted revolutionary attitude

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word is taken
revolutionary means turned around, so the word is read upward

parts.note: a pose is a stance or attitude

explanation.surface: A teller of tales first took up a radical stance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses POSE to give ESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabulist is a writer of fables, and this ancient Greek is the most famous one.

clue.text: Draw attention from cuts in European energy

indicators.note: in means the first piece goes inside the following pair of letters

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
clips are cuts, as with shears

explanation.surface: Budget cuts in European energy divert attention away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts CLIPS between the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: To overshadow something is to take attention away from it, just as one body blocks another's light.

clue.text: Hero old flame accepting a ring

indicators.note: accepting means the outer word takes the others inside it

parts.note: leman is an archaic word for a lover or sweetheart
ding is the sound of a bell, a ring

explanation.surface: A former sweetheart, a hero to someone, takes a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old flame' means an archaic word for a lover, not an ex-partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading man plays the principal male role, the hero of a film or play.

clue.text: Maybe stone wife shed to reveal figure?

indicators.note: shed means letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a stone, 14 pounds, is a unit of weight in Britain

explanation.surface: Losing a few stone reveals a wife's figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds; 'Maybe' marks it as an example. 'shed' removes the W.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a numeral, and eight is one of them.

clue.text: Down current unseen in Egyptian port

indicators.note: unseen means the letter is taken out of view

parts.note: Port Said is a port at the Suez Canal's northern end
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An invisible undercurrent in an Egyptian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down is feeling unhappy or low.

clue.text: Unenlightened period without Sun and Times?

parts.note: with no sunlight things are dark
ages are long times or eras

explanation.surface: Life without the Sun and The Times newspapers is unenlightened.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun and The Times are British newspapers, but here they are sunlight and eras.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval era in Europe is traditionally seen as lacking learning and culture.

clue.text: Fault is mended in narrow pipe

indicators.note: mended means the letters are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: A defect in a small pipe has been repaired.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is a narrow tube or abnormal passage, the word coming from Latin for pipe.

clue.text: Siren's beginning song with noise in island

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter is used
in means the noise goes inside the song

parts.note: an aria is a song in opera
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A siren starts singing noisily on an island, as in the Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardinia is a large Italian island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Woods monarch must leave to find game

indicators.note: must leave means these letters go out of the word

parts.note: Tiger Woods is the American golfer
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A royal must quit the woods to hunt game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woods' looks like forest but is the golfer Tiger Woods. Tig is the British children's chasing game, also called tag.
explanation.definitionFit: Tig is a playground chasing game, also known as tag or it.

clue.text: Lover's note penned by one seeking divorce?

definitions.note: Lover's stands for lover is, a noun phrase with the verb as a link

indicators.note: penned by means the note is enclosed inside the other word

parts.note: a parter, cryptically, is one who parts from a spouse

explanation.surface: A lover's letter written by someone wanting to divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a letter but is N; PARTER is a playful invented word for someone splitting up.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is a romantic companion or spouse, the one someone loves.

clue.text: Very friendly alien seen in copse

parts.note: thick as thieves: thick means very close or intimate
ET is the alien of the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A friendly alien is spotted in a small wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A thicket and a copse are both dense clumps of small trees or shrubs.

clue.text: Which letter is doubled in dissertation?

definitions.text: Which letter is doubled in dissertation?

parts.words: Which letter is doubled in dissertation?
parts.note: the honest reply names the one consonant that appears twice in that long word, and the reply, written without spaces, is itself an academic dissertation

explanation.surface: A spelling quiz question about a long word.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer the question in full: the doubled letter is the nineteenth of the alphabet. Run that sentence together and it means an academic dissertation.
explanation.definitionFit: A long academic essay written for a degree is a dissertation, the same thing.

clue.text: Water sprite that is lurking under seaweed

indicators.note: in a down clue, lurking under means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed
ie, id est, is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A water spirit hides beneath the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish folklore this shape-shifting water spirit, often a horse, haunts rivers and lochs.

clue.text: Selling rights his in continental country

indicators.note: in means his is set inside the country

parts.note: France is a country on the European continent

explanation.surface: A man's commercial licences in a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: A franchise is a licence granting the right to sell a company's goods or services.

clue.text: Large having consumed seconds: restrict diet

indicators.note: having consumed means the first word swallows the second

parts.note: fat means large in build

explanation.surface: A big eater who has had second helpings should cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: To fast is to eat little or nothing, limiting one's food.

clue.text: Lord who ran to seize power deal

indicators.note: to seize means the lord's name grabs the letter inside it

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the Olympic runner, became Lord Coe
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A peer who stood for office grabs power in a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' looks political but means running races: Lord Coe was an Olympic middle-distance champion.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope with something is to deal with or manage it.

clue.text: Frozen for example returning to top

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a top or cover

explanation.surface: A frozen example goes back to the lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid means icy cold, from Latin gelu, frost.

clue.text: Sea bass

definitions.meaning: a poetic term for the ocean
a bass voice is low in pitch

explanation.surface: A sea bass is a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea bass' reads as a fish but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetically the ocean is called this, and a low-pitched voice or note is also described so.

clue.text: Farm animals slowly escape — hard to stop that

indicators.note: to stop means the letter plugs a gap, sitting inside the word

parts.note: to seep is to leak out slowly
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Farm animals are slowly getting out, and it's hard to prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are farmed livestock; the word serves as a plural here.

clue.text: Musical by Rice one knocked back as unoriginal

indicators.note: knocked back means the assembled letters are reversed

parts.note: Evita is a musical
Tim Rice wrote the lyrics for Evita
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Tim Rice musical rejected as derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses EVITA + TIM + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that copies or imitates is lacking in originality.
